hints: The differential equation is separable: put all factors involving $x$ with $dx$ and all factors involving $t$ with $dt$.
Integrate $1/x$ with respect to $x$ and $ke^{-0.1t}$ with respect to $t$, taking care that integrating the exponential introduces a factor of $-10$.
Use the initial condition $x=20$ when $t=0$ to determine the integration constant, then rearrange to a relation between $\ln x$, $t$, and $k$.
walkthrough:
Separate variables in the differential equation $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = kx\mathrm{e}^{-0.1t}$:
$$\dfrac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x = k\mathrm{e}^{-0.1t}\,\mathrm{d}t$$
$$\int \dfrac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x = \int k\mathrm{e}^{-0.1t}\,\mathrm{d}t$$

Integrate the left-hand side with respect to $x$:
$$\int \dfrac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x = \ln x$$

Integrate the right-hand side with respect to $t$:
$$\int k\mathrm{e}^{-0.1t}\,\mathrm{d}t = \dfrac{k}{-0.1}\mathrm{e}^{-0.1t} = -10k\mathrm{e}^{-0.1t}$$

Combine the integrated terms with a constant of integration $C$:
$$\ln x = -10k\mathrm{e}^{-0.1t} + C$$

Substitute the initial condition $x = 20$ when $t = 0$ to find $C$:
$$\ln(20) = -10k\mathrm{e}^0 + C$$
$$\ln 20 = -10k + C \implies C = 10k + \ln 20$$

Substitute $C$ back into the equation and factor $10k$:
$$\ln x = -10k\mathrm{e}^{-0.1t} + 10k + \ln 20$$
$$\ln x = 10k(1 - \mathrm{e}^{-0.1t}) + \ln 20$$

ai_rubric.Solving Separable Differential Equations: Separates variables : $\int(1/x)dx=\int ke^{-0.1t}dt$; Derives term $-10ke^{-0.1t}$; Concludes with $\ln x=10k(1-e^{-0.1t})+\ln20$.

skill_tags: Applying Initial Conditions to Differential Equations

hints: Substitute the new data $x=40$ and $t=10$ into the relation obtained in part (a) to determine $k$.
Simplify using $e^{-0.1(10)}=e^{-1}$ and $\ln40-\ln20=\ln2$ before solving for $k$.
For the long-term amount, let $t\to\infty$, use $e^{-0.1t}\to0$, and then exponentiate the limiting value of $\ln x$ to obtain a numerical amount.
walkthrough:
Substitute $x = 40$ and $t = 10$ into the relation from part (a):
$$\ln(40) = 10k(1 - \mathrm{e}^{-0.1 \times 10}) + \ln 20$$
$$\ln 40 - \ln 20 = 10k(1 - \mathrm{e}^{-1})$$

Simplify the left-hand side using the quotient law of logarithms $\ln 40 - \ln 20 = \ln\left(\dfrac{40}{20}\right) = \ln 2$:
$$\ln 2 = 10k(1 - \mathrm{e}^{-1})$$

Determine the limiting value of $x$ as $t$ becomes very large ($t \to \infty$):
Since $-0.1 < 0$, $\mathrm{e}^{-0.1t} \to 0$ as $t \to \infty$.
Therefore:
$$\ln x \to 10k(1 - 0) + \ln 20 = 10k + \ln 20$$

Substitute $10k = 1.09654$ and solve for the limiting value of $x$:
$$x \to \mathrm{e}^{10k + \ln 20} = 20\mathrm{e}^{10k} = 20\mathrm{e}^{1.09654} \approx 20(2.99380) \approx 59.876$$

State the limiting value of $x$ correct to 3 significant figures:
$$x \to 59.9$$

ai_rubric.Interpreting Differential-Equation Solut: Taking $t\to\infty$ in the solved differential-equation model gives the limiting value $x\to59.9$.
